pure-announcement.rationale: This is the formal IETF Standards Track RFC itself, not a launch, release note, or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: The existing JSON Web Encryption concept only mentions JWT in passing, as one thing JWE can encrypt (nested JWTs); it does not cover JWT's own claims structure, registered claim names, or the signed-versus-encrypted choice, so a reader of it learns nothing about what this note defines.

unfalsifiable.rationale: It is the primary standard itself — the maximally checkable source, since it is what conformance is measured against.

durability.rationale: A decade-old IETF Standards Track RFC with no version numbers, pricing, or vendor feature matrix to churn — the format and its registered claim semantics are the stable reference point implementations converge on.

actionability.rationale: Defines exactly which claim names are already standardized (iss, sub, aud, exp, nbf, iat, jti) and the signed-versus-encrypted structural choice, letting a reader implement offline-verifiable, self-contained tokens directly from off-the-shelf libraries rather than inventing token semantics from scratch.

atomicity.rationale: One idea — a compact, URL-safe JSON claims format that can be signed and/or encrypted for offline verification — stated in a paragraph; the registered claims and security considerations are facets of that one format, not separate standalone concepts the way an unrelated policy catalog would be.
